turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You entered a zero on my son's essay before anyone picked up a phone to call me. I have until 4:40, Hale. Who decided, and on what basis?
"Ok" is not an answer, Hale. If you have nothing to show me, I'll walk down to the principal's office now.
I came straight from my office for this. Withdraw the zero, or tell me why you won't, because the principal's office is my next stop.
Ok what, Hale? Are you withdrawing the zero, yes or no?
I'm writing down that you said yes. I want it in an email before 4:40, with the zero gone and nothing on Owen's record.
Then the gradebook changes today, not tomorrow. And Owen hears it from you, Hale, privately, not from his phone in the middle of class.
Sorry. The essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet.
A minute ago you said ok to withdrawing the zero, and I wrote it down. Show me the line, and show me where you looked. A misquote is a citation error, Hale, not proof of anything else.
